text:
B: Alright? Can you hear me okay?
A: Yeah, hi. Karen.
B: Darren. Nice one. So, er, where are you? I'm in Bridgwater.
A: Taunton. I'm from Bridgwater originally, though. Mum's still there.
B: No way. Proper local, then. Whereabouts did you grow up?
A: Erm, up the Hamp end. Went to the comp there.
B: Same, sort of. Well, I was the other side. Funny, isn't it? All these people in the study and you get someone from down the road.
A: Yeah. Bit of a coincidence.
B: So what do you do, if you don't mind me asking?
A: I manage a charity shop. Hospice one, on the high street in Taunton.
B: Oh right. Must get some right stuff donated.
A: You've no idea. Someone gave us a full set of false teeth once. In a bag with some cardigans. Just sat there.
B: (laughs) What do you even do with that?
A: Bin. Can't exactly price them up. But you get good stuff too, designer bits people don't realise they've got. I can spot a label from across the back room now. What about you?
B: I'm a machine operator, packaging line at the food plant on the edge of town. Four on, four off, days and nights. People hear "factory" and they sort of switch off, but there's a lot of skill in it, the changeovers and that. I'm usually the one the supervisors come to when something's playing up. I keep my own notebook of all the fault codes, so, you know.
A: Sounds like you know what you're doing.
B: Try to. Going for team leader. Should've had it last year, but, er, you know how it is. Bit of favouritism.
A: Yeah, I know how that goes. Head office are just as bad. All those emails, "going forward", "touch base". Drives me mad.
B: Ha, "touch base". We get that and all.
A: Sorry, I'm going on.
B: No, you're alright. Do you get back to Bridgwater much, then?
A: Most Sundays. Roast at Mum's. She's on her own now, so.
B: Fair enough. I do our roast on Sundays. Bit particular about it, I'll be honest. Potatoes parboiled, roughed up properly. The wife says I write the timings down like it's a military operation.
A: (laughs) Do you actually write them down?
B: On the back of an envelope, yeah. Works, though.
A: I batch-cook mostly. Chilli, shepherd's pie, in the freezer. Easier on your own.
B: Makes sense. Here, you'll know Carnival, then. Still go?
A: Not for years. Dad used to take us. I loved it as a kid.
B: Best thing about the town, I reckon. People slag Bridgwater off, but come November the whole place turns out. I take photos of it now, actually, and the Levels, the starlings at Ham Wall. Got a second-hand Fuji a few years back.
A: Oh, that's nice. Is that one of yours on the calendar behind you?
B: No, that one's bought, but I've had a couple do alright in the local Facebook group. Couple of hundred likes on one of the murmurations.
A: That's good, that is. I just walk on the Quantocks, no camera. Bit of peace.
B: Quantocks is lovely. I take Bruno up there sometimes, my dog, but his legs aren't what they were —
